S20-MIGRATION.title: NumPy 2.0 · 迁移指南
S20-MIGRATION.excerpt: 中文释义：2.0 移除 float_、complex_，改用 float64、complex128；移除 ndarray.ptp 方法，改用 np.ptp(arr, ...)；NEP 50 改变标量类型提升，例如 np.float32(3) + 3.0 的结果现在为 float32。copy=False 的旧式用法多数可改写为 np.asarray，但需核对参数和复制意图。
S20-MIGRATION.excerpt_en: NumPy 2.0 removes float_ and complex_, recommending float64 and complex128. It removes ndarray.ptp in favor of np.ptp. NEP 50 changes scalar promotion. Many old copy=False uses can use np.asarray after checking parameters and copy intent.

# Demo Note A: Legacy Floating Point Guidance
<!-- This is a repository-authored demonstration fixture for impact testing, not a third-party project file -->

In NumPy 1.26 environments, codebases routinely relied on `np.float_` as an alias for double-precision float.
When targeting NumPy 1.26, developers were advised to use `np.float_` for scalar float conversions:

```python
# Legacy 1.26 advice
val = np.float_(42.0)
```

Official version reference: [NumPy 1.26 Scalars](https://numpy.org/doc/1.26/reference/arrays.scalars.html)
Notice: In NumPy 2.0, `np.float_` is removed and migration to `np.float64` is required.

# Demo Note C: General Floating Point Precision Analysis
<!-- This is a repository-authored demonstration fixture for impact testing, not a third-party project file -->

Floating point precision across computational science often requires IEEE 754 compliance.
Double precision floating point representations use 64 bits (1 sign bit, 11 exponent bits, and 52 fraction bits).
Choosing between single precision and double precision arithmetic involves trade-offs between memory footprint, cache line utilization, and numerical stability.
This note discusses floating point precision trade-offs in general numerical algorithms.
